Explanation, principles: (ア) steam expands in the nozzle and pressure energy becomes velocity energy, so the pressure falls. (イ) Constant blade-passage area means no further expansion in the blades, so inlet and outlet pressures are equal. (エ) The reaction turbine also expands steam in the moving blades. All three are correct.

Explanation, why each type suits its pressure range: (ウ) With no pressure difference across the moving blades, little steam leaks past the blade tips, so the impulse turbine suits high pressure. (オ) The reaction turbine has a pressure difference across the moving blades. In high-pressure stages the specific volume is small and the blades are short, so tip leakage is a larger share of the flow, and the reaction turbine therefore suits medium and low pressure. Both cause-and-effect explanations are correct.
